sections.overview: The blackmouth catshark is a small deep-water catshark of the northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean, in the family Pentanchidae.
sections.identification: It has a slender body, long anal fin, dark saddles and spots, pale underside, and a distinctively black mouth interior.
sections.habitat: It lives on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, usually at 200–500 m but reported from 55–2 000 m.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling invertebrates such as shrimp and cephalopods, alongside small bony fishes and other small sharks.
sections.behavior: It is a demersal, offshore species, and individuals show depth segregation by size, with adults and juveniles generally deeper than recruits.
sections.reproduction: It is oviparous; females may carry up to thirteen egg cases, and regional studies describe seasonal variation in reproduction.
sections.ecology: Galeus atlanticus and G. murinus are related catsharks in the same genus and useful comparisons, though their ranges and depth use differ.
sections.conservation: Shark Trust reports Least Concern assessments globally (2009) and regionally (2015–2016), while noting variable bycatch retention and fishery pressure.
